answer: A chameleon-hash signature uses a trapdoor hash where the holder of the trapdoor can find collisions, letting it adapt a signed message to a new one without invalidating the signature, while anyone without the trapdoor finds collisions infeasible. The signer signs the hash value, and the trapdoor holder can later swap the message while keeping the same hash. A pearl of trust travels on a voyage where only the trapdoor holder can rewrite the summit record, and outsiders see a valid signature either way. A farm without the trapdoor cannot rewrite claims, because each collision needs that secret.
